# Therapeutic Itinerary {.unnumbered}

## What It Is and Why Use It

**Patient Journey Mapping (PJM)** is a set of methods for visualizing and describing how people enter, move through, and exit services, combining visual maps, narratives, and tables that portray experiences, transitions, and interactions along the care pathway. Recent reviews highlight the growth of PJM since 2015, the variety of approaches, and its usefulness for identifying gaps and guiding new user-centered models of care—although methodological reporting remains inconsistent. [Patient journey mapping: emerging methods for understanding and improving patient experiences of health systems and services - PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38306596/){target="_blank"}

PJM directly connects with people-centered care and network integration agendas by making **explicit** the needs, emotions, goals, and barriers at each stage of the journey. This makes it a bridge between patient experience, process improvement, and health policy. [Integrated people-centred care - GLOBAL](https://www.who.int/health-topics/integrated-people-centered-care){target="_blank"}

---

## Most Commonly Used Methods and Artifacts

**Journey maps**: timeline with stages, touchpoints, emotions/pain points, expectations, and associated evidence. [Reporting and conducting patient journey mapping research in healthcare: A scoping review - PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36330555/){target="_blank"}

* **Service blueprinting**: adds "backstage" elements (processes, roles, ICT, rules), facilitating operational prioritization and the design of digital/omnichannel flows. [Using Journey Mapping and Service Blueprinting to Design Digital Health Behavior Change Innovations: A Scoping Review](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12061902/){target="_blank"}
* **Emotional/experience mapping**: maps emotional highs and lows to guide experience and safety interventions. [Lifestyle Medicine Accelerator – Co-design Toolkit](https://www.lifestylemedicineaccelerator.co.uk/s/LMA-Co-design-Toolkit.pdf){target="_blank"}
* **Process mapping/lean**: captures the "as is" with multidisciplinary teams; useful for finding waste, bottlenecks, and handoff risks. [Conventional process mapping - aqua.nhs.uk](https://aqua.nhs.uk/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/qsir-conventional-process-mapping.pdf){target="_blank"}
* **PJM + data**: integration with **process mining** (EHR) and **simulation** to quantify flows/times and test "what if…?" scenarios. [A Data-Driven Approach to Support the Understanding and Improvement of Patients' Journeys: A Case Study Using Electronic Health Records of an Emergency Department](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1098301522001978)
* **Co-design/EBCD**: uses narratives (patients/professionals) to co-create solutions; guides and evidence of impact are available. [Experience-Based Co-Design of Health Care Services](https://www.ihi.org/sites/default/files/2023-10/ExperienceBasedCoDesign_ImplementationGuide.pdf){target="_blank"}

The most recent methodological synthesis proposes **six steps** for conducting PJM, illustrated with cardiovascular cases: define objective/scope; collect data; build the map; identify opportunities; co-create solutions; and plan evaluation/implementation. [Patient journey mapping: emerging methods for understanding and improving patient experiences of health systems and services - PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38306596/){target="_blank"}

---

## Evidence and Applied Cases (Service Improvement and Model of Care)

* **Emergency department access and experience**: journey maps were used to **improve communication** with patients/families in the ED and guide flow changes; reviews on **ED flow** show that reducing times is associated with better outcomes, and simulation studies show significant decreases in triage times when design is adjusted based on the map. [The patient journey map: Improving the emergency department communication experience for patients and their family and friends](https://cjen.ca/index.php/cjen/article/view/131){target="_blank"}
* **Oncology journey**: mappings have identified gaps in screening-diagnosis-treatment stages, pointing to navigation solutions, pre-consultation preparation, and results communication; a specific review on **breast cancer** systematizes PJM uses for improving care pathways. [Breast cancer patient experiences through a journey map](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0257680&utm_source=chatgpt.com){target="_blank"}
* **Chronic and digital care**: blueprinting + journey mapping have been applied to **digital interventions** for behavior change and self-care, structuring support points, channels (app/phone/in-person), and team integrations. [Using Journey Mapping and Service Blueprinting to Design Digital Health Behavior Change Innovations: A Scoping Review](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12061902/){target="_blank"}
* **Human-centered design and QI**: studies and guides show PJM as a trigger for **improvement focus** (prioritization) and patient-centered design; a classic patient-centered mapping case (mixed methods) directed QI efforts toward experience. [Creation of a Patient-Centered Journey Map to Improve the Patient Experience: A Mixed Methods Approach](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6978601/){target="_blank"}
* **Surveillance and viral hepatitis (Asia)**: qualitative PJM methodology in Vietnam and the Philippines informed the **co-design** of people-centered interventions adapted to local context. [Putting people at the center: methods for patient journey mapping of viral hepatitis services across two LMICs in the Asia Pacific](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11934455/){target="_blank"}

---

## How to Apply (Practical Roadmap for Redesigning the Itinerary)

1. **Define the problem, scope, and goals**
Choose the care pathway (e.g., "suspicion → diagnosis → treatment initiation") and indicators (time to diagnosis, absenteeism, continuity). Use a **logic model** and "Triple/Quadruple Aim" objectives. Draw on process guides to frame the improvement. [Process mapping, analysis and redesign](https://www.england.nhs.uk/improvement-hub/wp-content/uploads/sites/44/2017/11/ILG-1.2-Process-Mapping-Analysis-and-Redesign.pdf){target="_blank"}

2. **Collect mixed data (qualitative + operational)**
Interviews/observation (patients, caregivers, professionals), system data (times, referrals), complaints, and PREMs/PROMs (e.g., **OECD PaRIS** in PHC). [Patient-Reported Indicator Surveys](https://www.oecd.org/en/about/programmes/patient-reported-indicator-surveys-paris.html){target="_blank"}

3. **Build the map(s)**

* **Journey map** (stages, emotions, barriers, capabilities).
* **Service blueprint** (frontstage/backstage, actors, ICT, rules).
* **Process map** ("as is") with an expanded team (PHC, specialized care, regulation). [Using Journey Mapping and Service Blueprinting to Design Digital Health Behavior Change Innovations: A Scoping Review](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12061902/){target="_blank"}

4. **Equity and risk analysis**
Apply **PROGRESS-Plus** (residence, race/ethnicity, occupation, gender, education, income, social capital, disability, etc.) to see where the itinerary **fails the most**; identify safety risks at handoffs. [Reporting and conducting patient journey mapping research in healthcare: A scoping review - PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36330555/){target="_blank"}

5. **Co-create solutions and prioritize**
Use **EBCD**/workshops to generate and test countermeasures (pathway navigation; segmented checklists and messages; "one-stop" scheduling; active follow-up for no-shows; hybrid digital/in-person flows). **Blueprints** help estimate feasibility and dependencies. [Experience-Based Co-Design of Health Care Services](https://www.ihi.org/sites/default/files/2023-10/ExperienceBasedCoDesign_ImplementationGuide.pdf){target="_blank"}

6. **Pilot, measure, and learn (LHS)**
Implement rapid tests (PDSA) and integrate journey data into a **Learning Health System** — cycles of collection → analysis → feedback → adjustment. Connect **PREMs/PROMs** (PaRIS) to flow metrics (lead time, successful handoffs) and outcomes. [Exploring Patient Journey Mapping and the Learning Health System: Scoping Review](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36848189/){target="_blank"}

7. **Scale and sustain**
Standards, kits, and EBCD and mapping toolkits support replication and training of clinical/management teams. [Experience-based co-design toolkit](https://www.kingsfund.org.uk/insight-and-analysis/projects/experience-based-co-design-toolkit){target="_blank"}

## Common Pitfalls and How to Mitigate Them

* **Heterogeneous reporting/execution** → adopt methodological checklists (objective, data, personas/journeys, validation, indicators). [Reporting and conducting patient journey mapping research in healthcare: A scoping review - PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36330555/){target="_blank"}
* **Focus only on the "average" patient** → include **priority populations** and structural barriers (transportation, income, connectivity), reflecting these in the map and solutions. [Reporting and conducting patient journey mapping research in healthcare: A scoping review - PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36330555/){target="_blank"}
* **Map without change** → connect PJM to **improvement methods** (Lean, PDSA), clinical governance, and implementation budgets. [Conventional process mapping - aqua.nhs.uk](https://aqua.nhs.uk/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/qsir-conventional-process-mapping.pdf){target="_blank"}
* **Non-actionable solutions** → complement with **blueprints** and, when possible, **process mining/simulation** to test capacity, queues, and trade-offs before scaling. [Using Journey Mapping and Service Blueprinting to Design Digital Health Behavior Change Innovations: A Scoping Review](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12061902/){target="_blank"}

## Essential References (Annotated Selection)

* **Bulto LN et al.** Patient journey mapping — overview and **six steps**; foundation for structuring PJM projects. Eur J Cardiovasc Nurs. 2024. [Patient journey mapping: emerging methods for understanding and improving patient experiences of health systems and services - PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38306596/){target="_blank"}
* **Davies EL et al.** Scoping review on **how to conduct and report** PJM; shows acceleration in use and standardization gaps. J Adv Nurs. 2023. [Reporting and conducting patient journey mapping research in healthcare: A scoping review - PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36330555/){target="_blank"}
* **Voorheis P et al.** Scoping review on **journey mapping + service blueprinting** in digital behavior change interventions. 2025. [Using Journey Mapping and Service Blueprinting to Design Digital Health Behavior Change Innovations: A Scoping Review](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12061902/){target="_blank"}
* **Philpot LM et al.** Case of a **patient-centered map** (mixed methods) to focus experience improvements. 2019. [Creation of a Patient-Centered Journey Map to Improve the Patient Experience: A Mixed Methods Approach](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6978601/){target="_blank"}
* **Duan Y et al.** PJM applications in the **breast cancer care pathway** (synthesis of uses and lessons). BMJ Open. 2025. [Application of patient journey mapping in patients with breast cancer: a scoping review](https://bmjopen.bmj.com/content/15/10/e103201){target="_blank"}
* **Holt B et al.** Qualitative PJM methodology for viral hepatitis (Vietnam/Philippines) focused on **co-design** and context. 2025. [Putting people at the center: methods for patient journey mapping of viral hepatitis services across two LMICs in the Asia Pacific](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11934455/){target="_blank"}
* **IHI / King's Fund / Point of Care**. **EBCD** guides (experience-based co-design) — step-by-step, cases, and tools. [Experience-Based Co-Design of Health Care Services](https://www.ihi.org/sites/default/files/2023-10/ExperienceBasedCoDesign_ImplementationGuide.pdf){target="_blank"}
* **NHS England / AQuA**. **Process mapping** guides for mapping journeys/processes and initiating improvements safely. [Process mapping, analysis and redesign](https://www.england.nhs.uk/improvement-hub/wp-content/uploads/sites/44/2017/11/ILG-1.2-Process-Mapping-Analysis-and-Redesign.pdf){target="_blank"}
* **OECD PaRIS**. Concept, analytical plan, and field results — **PREMs/PROMs** for monitoring experience and outcomes in PHC. [Data analysis plan of the OECD PaRIS survey](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11157922/){target="_blank"}
* **Process mining / simulation**. Analytical complements to enrich PJM and test scenarios. [A Data-Driven Approach to Support the Understanding and Improvement of Patients' Journeys: A Case Study Using Electronic Health Records of an Emergency Department](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1098301522001978){target="_blank"}

---

## In Summary (Practical Lessons)

* Use PJM to **align teams** around itinerary goals (time to diagnosis; continuity; experience; equity).
* **Mix methods**: journey + blueprint + process + data (PREMs/PROMs, EHR, times) + co-design.
* **Design for equity** from the start (PROGRESS-Plus) and test **capacity/flow** before scaling.
* **Measure and learn**: integrate PJM into a **Learning Health System** with PDSA cycles and actionable indicators. [Exploring Patient Journey Mapping and the Learning Health System: Scoping Review](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36848189/){target="_blank"}
